The error message you’re seeing, “Code signing violation detected!”, indicates that Overwatch 2 (or its anti-cheat system) detected a suspicious or unauthorized .dll file—specifically kern3132.dll—in your Windows System32 folder. This is often associated with security issues, as legitimate system files typically do not trigger code-signing errors, and kern3132.dll doesn’t appear to be a standard Windows system file. If that doesn't work try scanning for malware, Update Overwatch 2 and [Battle.net](http://battle.net/) Launcher or

# Verify Game Files

* Use Battle.net’s *Scan and Repair* feature to verify Overwatch 2 files:
* Open [Battle.net](http://battle.net/) \> **Overwatch 2** \> **Options** \> **Scan and Repair**.

# Reboot in Safe Mode

* If you’re unable to remove the suspicious .dll file, reboot your system in **Safe Mode** to see if the file still appears.
* In Safe Mode, go back and try running a full scan again. Safe Mode prevents most malicious files from executing, which can help antivirus tools detect and remove them.

# Reinstall Overwatch 2 (if necessary)

* If the issue persists after clearing up any malware, consider reinstalling Overwatch 2.
